People's Majlis Committee Minutes

22nd Meeting of the Public Finance Committee

19 October 2026

Venue of the meeting: People's Majlis A Building (Committee Room 10)

Start time: 10:39

{Presided by the Deputy Chair of the Committee; Member for Eydhafushi constituency, Ahmed Saleem}

The Chair speaking:

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم. 22nd meeting of the Public Finance Committee. Agenda item 1 - Reviewing the following matters submitted by private parties. The matter submitted sharing concerns regarding the change to the salaries of legal professionals under the State Pay Framework standards and the amendments made to salaries. I open the floor to members on this matter.

The secretariat speaking:

You see, this matter has been submitted by 3 parties. They say that due to the change in the legal framework, their salaries have decreased. At that time the committee decided to obtain further information from the Civil Service Commission and the Finance Ministry. We have also received replies from the National Pay Commission and the Civil Service Commission. In the Civil Service Commission's letter they noted that, in the salary structure and benefits for legal officers in effect before 1 November 2005, the service allowance was set differently for employees working in the atolls and employees working in Malé. Therefore, under the new salary structure that came into effect on 1 November 2025, it has been noted that the salaries and benefits of employees among the legal officer ranks who were moved to Public Service Rank 5 and Public Service Rank 6 have decreased. They have also sent the extent of the salary decrease in the details in the sheets included in this letter. Along with that, they noted that offices were informed by this commission's circular No. 2025/9 dated 9 November 2025 to submit for allowances to be arranged, for those whose salaries decreased, under the standard for granting the migration allowance included in the State Pay Framework standards. And that, following this notice, when offices submit to the National Pay Commission, the migration allowance is being arranged. The Finance Ministry and the National Pay Commission have also replied in the same manner. So, for them, we will now have

[stamp]

a reply ready, referring to their letter and with the information in it, a letter drafted saying that the migration allowance has been arranged in that way, ready to reply from our side. Shall we read out the letter? The draft letter?

The Chair speaking:

Next is the matter submitted by the staff of the Information Commissioner's Office sharing their concerns because it has been decided to stop the living allowance that had been given to the staff of that office and to recover from the staff the money given to them as living allowance. The matter stating that the pension received on reaching 65 years of age, after 20 years of service, has been cut off. This a little...

The secretariat speaking:

The committee received a letter from the staff, together with a petition. Those two matters have been submitted regarding the Information Commission Office, in connection with the changes made to their salaries. At that time we had clarified information from the Information Commission Office on this matter. And we had also clarified information from the Finance Ministry. The actual issue arose because in the 2023 compliance audit report of the Information Commission Office, the Auditor General noted that an allowance not approved by the National Pay Commission had been given, so that money should be recovered. So in this matter, since the matter was received, when we clarified information from the Information Commission Office, they noted, in their reply letter from the Information Commission Office they noted, that because an allowance was given to the staff of the Information Commission Office as living allowance from 2024 without obtaining approval from the National Pay Commission, the audit report advised obtaining the approval needed to give the allowance. Following that, the National Pay Commission and the Ministry of Finance and Planning were requested for approval to arrange the allowance. However, that approval

[stamp]

has not been obtained. Secondly, the audit report advised recovering the money paid to staff as living allowance, and proceeding in consultation with the Ministry of Finance and Planning regarding how to recover that money. Under the correspondence made in this regard, in accordance with that ministry's instruction, payment of the allowance to staff has been stopped from October 2025. And that ministry said that it would share with this office how to proceed in recovering the money paid to staff. However, no further guidance has been given by that ministry on this matter so far, you see, that is about the Finance Ministry. And the Information Commission Office has also informed that the work of recovering that money from the staff has not been carried forward. It is further stated that the decision to give living allowance to the staff of the Information Commission Office was made because, in addition to the living allowance for staff being included in this office's budget passed by the People's Majlis in 2024, the Ministry of Finance and Planning had approved the staff salaries including the allowance. They say those budget codes were included and the budget was approved. That is why the allowance was given, they say. Then in connection with that, the Finance Ministry also, in the Finance Ministry's reply, stated that no such approval had been given to give them the allowance. That being so, they took the allowance in breach of the regulations. We also briefly shared this matter with the Chair. The Chair advised replying to them on this matter by setting out and explaining what the law and regulations say. In addition, he said to send a letter to the Finance Ministry, right? That is to take action against those who acted in that way. Then in addition to that; so, we will now have a letter drafted to the Finance Ministry in that way, you see. And in addition to that, we are also writing a separate letter to the Information Commission Office, you see, saying that under the law, for example, salaries must be set by the Pay Commission. In addition, if any extra money has been paid, since that is money that must be recovered for the State, to arrange the recovery of that money and to inform the Public Finance Committee of the procedure for doing so, a separate letter

[stamp]

written to the Information Commission, and then for them, for the two staff members who submitted the matter, to write the details of how these things took place.

The Chair speaking:

That is what I am saying too. Those who gave it must not give anything contrary to government regulations, isn't it? Isn't that so? So there must also be action to be taken against those who gave it contrary to that procedure. Isn't that so? When giving it, they will of course take it when it is given, won't they. So, we will conclude the matter that way. (After a short while) Mamdooh, propose on these two as well.

Member for Funadhoo constituency Mohamed Mamdooh speaking:

Thank you, Chair. I propose, on both these matters, that a written reply be given as discussed in this committee.

Member for Kelaa constituency Abdulla Shareef speaking:

I second Mamdooh's proposal.

The Chair speaking:

Those in favour please vote. (Voting) Next is agenda item 2 - Sharing with the committee information on the loans below. State Trading Organization; is there still? The matter submitted stating that the pension received on reaching 65 years of age, after 20 years of service, has been cut off.

Member for Funadhoo constituency Mohamed Mamdooh speaking:

[stamp]

Thank you, Chair. On the matter just submitted, I propose that this committee give a written reply to this party, taking into account the information given by the Pension Office and the related offices.

Member for Kelaa constituency Abdulla Shareef speaking:

I second Mamdooh's proposal.

The Chair speaking:

Next is agenda item 2 - Sharing with the committee information on the loans below. Information regarding the sovereign guarantee issued by the government for the one hundred million US dollar senior term credit facility taken by OQ Trading Limited (OQT) to arrange the funds needed for the internal funding of State Trading Organization (STO). That is one. That is, anything regarding that; (After a short while) Information regarding the guarantee issued by the government for the twenty-five million US dollar sovereign murabaha financing facility signed with the International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation (ITFC) to obtain funds needed for goods imported by State Trading Organization (STO). These are things shared just for information. Next is information regarding the loan signed between the Maldives government and ADB to obtain fifty million US dollars needed for the "Energy Security Emergency Assistance Project" arranged to be carried out in the Maldives with the assistance of the Asian Development Bank (ADB). Next is information regarding the sovereign guarantee issued by the government for Maldives Industrial Fisheries Company Limited (MIFCO) to take a forty-four million US dollar demand loan facility and a two hundred million Maldivian rufiyaa overdraft facility through Bank of Maldives, to arrange funds needed for the company's cash flow and to repay the loan taken through SME Digital. Next is Maldives Airports Company Limited (MACL), to take a twenty-eight million US dollar facility, with Vitol Apac Capital Private

[stamp]

Limited (Vitol), the guarantee issued by the Maldives government for the facility signed. That concludes the information on all these loans. 3- Sharing with the committee the following letters received by the committee. Sharing with the committee the letter sent by the Auditor General's Office stating that the office has, for the first time, obtained membership of the board of the INTOSAI Development Initiative (IDI), the capacity-building body of the International Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions (INTOSAI). (After a short while) Next is sharing with the committee the matter submitted stating that a person in a senior position at Maldives Gas Private Limited is repeatedly violating ethics and governance standards, regulations on fiduciary duty and conflicts of interest, as well as the company's internal control frameworks.

The secretariat speaking:

You see, this matter was sent to two committees, the SOE Committee and the Public Finance Committee. Since it is a matter concerning the Secretary General of Maldives Gas Private Limited, this matter has been looked into by that committee, the SOE Committee. A decision has also been reached. Yes! So, the matter is to be filed in the Public Finance Committee, you see.

The Chair speaking:

Next is sharing with the committee the letter sent by a private party to the Anti-Corruption Commission, copied to the People's Majlis Secretariat, requesting investigation of corruption-related matters concerning a person in a senior position at GA. Atoll Hospital.

(After a short while)

The secretariat speaking:

Regarding the matter of Hoarafushi council leasing a five thousand square foot plot of land to The Hawks Private Limited for oil trading in Hoarafushi, I have submitted my concerns to the Anti-Corruption

[stamp]

Commission. Then the Anti-Corruption Commission decided that this matter is a matter with an issue, (After a short while) okay. Yes! The letter sent by the Anti-Corruption, right? I read out the other letter, you see. Sorry, you see. Now, this matter is a matter submitted regarding a person who is currently still in the post of Director of GA. Atoll Hospital. In the matter they submitted, they mainly noted that this person, who was in the post of Kooddoo Fisheries junior officer, actually obtained the post by falsifying documents. By submitting documents for a higher post than that. In addition to that, they also noted that for a trip made by launch to carry an oxygen cylinder for use at G. Atoll, G. Atoll Hospital, on a day of good weather it was made out to be a day of bad weather, and for the trip made for fifteen thousand rufiyaa, later thirty, the quotation documents were destroyed and a quotation of thirty thousand rufiyaa was made, falsifying State documents so that he would receive a direct financial benefit. So this matter is one they sent to the Anti-Corruption Commission and copied to us at the Public Finance Committee. So, it will be filed, you see.

The Chair speaking:

I am sharing with the committee the letter sent by a private party to the Prosecutor General's Office, copied to the People's Majlis Secretariat, regarding the matter of the island council leasing a five thousand square foot plot of land to The Hawks Private Limited for oil trading in HA. Hoarafushi.

The secretariat speaking:

This is the matter I just briefed, you see. In it they noted that when they sent the Hawks matter to the Anti-Corruption Commission, it was sent to the PG to look into, and the PG Office, the Anti-Corruption Commission gives a statement; two or three days after the Anti-Corruption Commission released the statement I mentioned, news was heard on the island that the Prosecutor General's Office had concluded the matter there and then. And further in this regard, that every person accused in the matter was fined one hundred

[stamp]

rufiyaa and given advice and the matter concluded, as heard by word of mouth. So when the matter was concluded in that way, they submitted the matter as a complaint. Yes! To the Prosecutor General's Office, then this the Prosecutor; actually, since this matter was sent to the Public Finance Committee, if there is such a matter concerning the Prosecutor General, we should actually send this matter to the Judiciary Committee. The committee should conclude this matter as a matter concerning the Prosecutor General by sending it to the Judiciary Committee actually; (Members consulting off the record) The matters on the agenda are here, there are still many matters shared and concluded in just this way.

The Chair speaking:

The rest is for tomorrow.

The secretariat speaking:

There will be an ACC meeting tomorrow, right? Tuesday, there will be an ACC meeting tomorrow.

The Chair speaking:

Let us take that part after the Tuesday meeting! That concludes everything on today's agenda. So, I will conclude the committee at this point, you see. Thank you.

[stamp]
